Acoustic modeling of sequential spaces: A parametric study
Tingting Yang, Jian Kang*
Institute for Environmental Design and Engineering, The Bartlett, University College London, Central House, 14 Upper Woburn Place, London, WC1H 0NN, United
Kingdom
A R T I C L E I N F O A B S T R A C T
Keywords: Sound field modeling of sequential spaces is required for large-scale public buildings. A finite element model
Acoustic simulation comprising five successive rooms was used for a parametric study considering, contextual factors (opening
Sound field modeling dimension and position, number of rooms), acoustic (absorption coefficient and distribution) and source factors
Parametric study
(directional radiation from the opening and an additional source), with the following results: (i) In rooms with
Finite element method

Sequential spaces
Coupled rooms rooms is smaller with larger opening dimensions. The opening position has a significant impact only for rooms
with low absorption. (ii) The level differences between rooms are larger for oblique than horizontal radiation,
especially for rooms close to the source. With an additional source (e.g., a heating, ventilation, and air condi-
tioning system or human speech) in a room, the level in that room will be maintained or reduced by approxi-
mately ~10 dB with increasing opening dimensions for high or low room absorption, respectively, whereas the
levels in other rooms increase for high room absorption. (iii) Changes to low absorption coefficients have more
significant effects. For a given absorption amount, the difference in average SPL in a room between uniform and
nonuniform absorption distribution are greater with smaller opening dimensions. (iv) The effect on the average
SPL in the first receiving room, caused by adding more sequential rooms is less when the absorption in those
rooms is high (e.g., an absorption coefficient of 0.5), and the maximum difference with different absorption
coefficients is ~6 dB, depending on the number of rooms.
